origins: A diagnosis, a flare, or a body that no longer cooperates can feel like treachery from the one thing we thought we could count on. Anger and grief at the body are natural, and over time they can turn into resentment, fear, or a sense of being at war with ourselves.
teaches: The psalmist says, “I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.” Paul writes, “Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.” “My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.” Our bodies live in a fallen world and wear down, but they are still gifts from God and we are still His. You can grieve what has been lost without making your body the enemy.
self_statements: I am at war with myself.
I hate what it has become.
errors: Seeing my body as either perfect or traitor.
Predicting that my body will keep failing.
Feeling let down and concluding it is hostile.
questions: What did I expect my body to do that it can no longer do?
What does my body still do for me each day?
How would I speak to a friend whose body is failing?
What does Scripture say about the body in a fallen world?
What would it look like to be gentle with my body?
truth: My body is part of a fallen world, yet it is God’s gift and I am His. I can grieve my losses, care for my body kindly, and trust God as the strength of my heart.
hw_truths: I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
My inner self is renewed daily.
God is the strength of my heart.
My body is a gift to steward.
I can be gentle with myself.
log: Each day, thank God for one thing your body did.
actions: List ten things it still does.
prayer: Lord, my body has changed and I am angry and afraid. Teach me to grieve honestly, care for it gently, and rely on You as the strength of my heart. Amen.
